t: What Does The Name Heay Mean?
s: In English contexts it most plausibly derives from Hay/Hey, surnames rooted in Middle English haye/heaȝe meaning “enclosure, hedge,” or from locative names tied to places called Hay or Hey, hence “one who lives by the hedge/enclosure” or “dweller at the high place” (the latter from Old English hēah, “high”). In Scots and Anglo-Norman lines, Hay traces to the de la Haye family (from La Haye, “the hedge/enclosure” in Norman French). As a given name, Heay may be a modern respelling influenced by the popularity of Hayley/Haylee or by Asian romanizations that render initial aspirates and vowels compactly.
